\section{Results}
\subsection{Base-case solution and policy comparison}
Table~\ref{tab:policy-comparison} reports the available 20 and 300~MW results. All values use the same representative-horizon annualisation convention.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Available LCOH and grid metrics under alternative RES policies.}
\label{tab:policy-comparison}
\begin{tabular}{r l r r r r}
\toprule
Stage (MW) & Policy & LCOH (EUR/kg) & RES (MW) & Max loading (\%) & Min voltage (p.u.) \\ \midrule
20 & Grid-only & 1.853 & 0.0 & 0.00 & 0.950 \\
20 & Compulsory RES & 1.886 & 20.0 & 10.43 & 0.950 \\
300 & Grid-only & 1.625 & 0.0 & 0.00 & 0.950 \\
300 & Compulsory RES & 6.981 & 300.0 & 1.71 & 0.950 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The compulsory-RES policy requires at least one RES connection and RES nameplate capacity equal to the electrolyser rating. The grid-only case is retained as a counterfactual and must not be interpreted as a green-hydrogen design.

\subsection{Grid impact}
The corrected voltage formulation stores squared voltage in kV$^2$ and reports post-processed magnitudes in per unit. The saved voltage and loading figures are therefore directly comparable with the stated operating limits.
